title: Isaac
lead: The son of Abraham and Sarah born in their old age, whose name means "he laughs." He was bound on the altar on Mount Moriah, married Rebekah, and became the father of Esau and Jacob. The New Testament calls him the child of promise (Romans 9:7–9; Galatians 4:28) and remembers his blessing of his sons as an act of faith (Hebrews 11:20).

sections.b: Isaac's birth is promised and laughed at (Genesis 17:17–19; 18:12–15) and his name, "he laughs," recalls it (21:6). He is bound on the altar at Moriah and spared (22:1–19), marries Rebekah (ch. 24), and blesses his sons (ch. 27). Later Israel calls God "the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob" (Exodus 3:6), and Amos even uses Isaac's name for the northern kingdom (Amos 7:9, 16). In the New Testament Isaac is the child of promise (Romans 9:7–9; Galatians 4:28). Hebrews says Abraham offered him believing that God could raise the dead (Hebrews 11:17–19), and James uses the same scene to show faith working with deeds (James 2:21). Jesus answers the Sadducees with "I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob" (Matthew 22:32).
